A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UnLoc and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial changes in formatting and content placement.

before.justification: V1 reports original localization, depth-prediction, runtime, ablation, and generalization results on Gibson, Structured3D, and LaMAR, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of trajectory refinement and alternative uncertainty distributions.

M1.justification: Section 3.8 adds an inference stage absent from v1: reconstructing the last ten poses from the final estimate and optimizing a global SE(2) correction using uncertainty-weighted depth residuals. The existing encoder, masked attention, Laplace matching, histogram filter, and training loss remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gibson, full and cropped LaMAR HGE, LaMAR CAB generalization/fine-tuning, and Structured3D single-frame localization. Structured3D and the single-frame analysis move to the appendix in v2; they are not removed. Newly described lighting and occlusion conditions clarify existing test sessions.

E2.justification: Appendix Table 11 adds a Gaussian-uncertainty UnLoc comparator motivated by Roessle et al. (2022). Existing localization comparators, including F3Loc mono/fusion, LASER, and PF-Net, are retained. The '+Depth Anything v2' rows match v1's uncertainty-free variant.

E3.justification: V2 Table 4 extends CAB evaluation at the 1 m threshold to shorter sequences; v1 reports that threshold only for length 100, with shorter CAB sequences evaluated at 2 m in the appendix. The new distribution comparison specifies Depth Anything v2 Small without post-processing. Existing training settings, splits, and main Gibson/HGE metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds with/without-refinement comparisons across Gibson, full/cropped HGE, and CAB, and directly tests Laplace versus Gaussian uncertainty in Appendix A.2.4. These substantially expand component validation. Existing encoder, single-frame, fine-tuning, update-frequency, and grid-resolution studies remain; the separate qualitative example in v1 Figure 5 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed experiments, confidence intervals, or significance tests for localization results. The expanded discussion and comparison of predicted depth uncertainty concern model outputs, not statistical uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add refined-method results: 15-frame success reaches 81.3% on Gibson and 50.6% on full HGE, alongside retained unrefined scores of 65.3% and 20.0%. CAB sequential results are revised and Gaussian-comparison results are added. These concern changed method variants. V2 also contains an unresolved discrepancy: the apparently matching Small-encoder Laplace setting scores 5.9% at T=15 in Table 5 but 4.7% in Table 11.

T1.justification: New Equations 6–8 formally define backward trajectory reconstruction, the SE(2) correction, and its uncertainty-weighted L1 objective. This is a limited mathematical extension; the existing matching, motion, filtering, and training formulations are retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain uncertainty-aware floorplan depth and pretrained monodepth encoders. V2 extends the claimed role of uncertainty to post-processing optimization and strengthens the abstract's 15-frame HGE improvement from 16.7-fold to 42.2-fold. The 100-frame 2.7-fold claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the modeled uncertainty as aleatoric and leaves epistemic uncertainty for future work. It qualifies the ground-truth-depth upper bound when refinement is applied and acknowledges the absence of independent 2D pose ground truth in Appendix A.1.2. Existing generalization and fine-tuning interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1.2 newly documents affine alignment using four doorways, pose conversion, split-selection rationale, and test-session conditions. V2 supplies a code/model access link and availability statement, plus the refinement window and runtime. The original training recipe remains, although the brief Structured3D setup description is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work gains a substantial discussion of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty, positioning UnLoc against prior uncertainty-estimation approaches, including Gaussian depth models. It also adds language/scene-graph localization and OrienterNet. This expands substantive research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites selected contribution and results paragraphs, renames variants, moves single-frame analysis from Section 4.2 to Appendix A.2.1, and adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with resized and repositioned displays. Tables gain refinement rows, the main CAB table changes structure, and Table 11 is added. Figure 2 is redrawn, v1 Figure 5 is removed, and the remaining qualitative figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens methodological support and reproducibility: it defines and ablates trajectory refinement, tests the uncertainty-distribution choice, and addresses v1's missing explanation of LaMAR pose alignment and split selection. Retaining unrefined results makes the added component's benefits assessable. The reported 0.96-second refinement cost and the isolated Tables 5/11 discrepancy limit the gains, but do not outweigh the stronger validation and documentation.
